extras.what: Exact whole-cent checks on the original JSON number text, safe-integer limits on amounts and resulting balances, BigInt arithmetic
extras.why: Rejects amounts JSON would round to an integer (1.00000000000000001) and keeps large sums exact; no lost cents.

extras.what: Startup validation of the whole saved ledger (each expense must reconcile; any bad record refuses startup and leaves the file intact)
extras.why: Never presents or overwrites a damaged ledger; the cost is that a hand-edited file of another shape will not load, which the inventory allows.

extras.what: Strict UTF-8 decoding of request bodies (malformed bytes -> 400)
extras.why: Stops a malformed byte from silently matching or creating a name with a replacement character.

extras.what: Preserving owner-only (0600) permission bits across snapshot replacement
extras.why: Not asked; harmless. Group-readable files (0640) still fall back to the umask, which the README states.

extras.what: PORT validation: refuses to start unless PORT is a decimal 1-65535
extras.why: A clear startup error instead of listening on a random port; port 0 is refused.

extras.what: Builder acceptance harness (clause-by-clause checks) and the builders' working notes shipped in the product
extras.why: Not run by node --test and not needed to run the service; extra material for a maintainer to sort out.

spec_notes: ratchet/spec.md maps every stated requirement to a clause (C-1..C-41) and nothing in it contradicts the request. It marks the request's gaps as "Open:" (port validation C-2, missing file C-3, id rules C-4, 409 vs 400 C-5, mixed member lists C-6, safe-integer range C-13, invalid-share status C-20, crash recovery C-37), and the builders then decided each one in plan.md rather than in the spec. Several decisions sit in ordinary clause lines attributed to the request or "implied": C-13 refuses the string "1", C-20 refuses negative and fractional shares, C-39/C-40 fix the concurrency outcomes. Clauses that come from the builders' own discoveries pin choices a correct product need not share: C-42 strict UTF-8 rejection, C-43 500 on a failed save, C-44/C-47 refusing to start on a malformed or inconsistent file (renaming it aside and starting empty is also acceptable), C-46/C-50 file permission preservation, C-49 interleaving of pending uploads. The spec states two clauses the delivered product does not meet, and the builders' own delta-3.md records both as not kept: C-48 (ids that get 201 must be reachable at any accepted length; 20,000-character ids get 431) and C-50 (0640 ledgers become 0644).
tests_notes: The suite has 13 large scenario tests, each covering many behaviours, so one failure does not point to one item: "rejects invalid expenses ..." alone carries S-17, S-20..S-25 and S-33, and was the only failing test for four different mutations. Tests tied to internals: "inconsistent expenses invalidate the entire saved ledger" edits the snapshot layout directly (wrongSum.groups[1].expenses[0].shares[1], string-replacing '"shares":[0,1]'); startServer waits for the exact stdout line "Listening on port <n>". Tests that would fail on another correct build of this request: the startup-refusal tests (a build that renames a bad file aside and starts empty is acceptable per U-10), the owner-only permission test (not requested), "failed saves ..." (expects 500 when the data directory is moved; a build that recreates the directory would succeed), the malformed UTF-8 test (a lossy decoder is not forbidden), "keeps remainder order ..." (expects cents written 6.00e0 to be accepted and 4294967297 to be exact), and the interrupted-upload test, which expects a particular interleaving of a pending upload with a completed one. Untested: syntactically broken JSON, missing payer/cents/split/id, encoded or awkward group ids, duplicate id with invalid members, and more than three concurrent writers.
maintainer: The whole-cent validation re-parses the raw body with a regex (parseNumberTokens) and walks a second "source" tree in step with the parsed one (source.cents, source.shares[member], source.groups[i].expenses[j].shares[k]); any change to the request or file shape has to keep both trees and the regex in step, and a slip there silently accepts rounded fractions or crashes. Ordering of writes depends on commit() running synchronously after the body is read; adding any await between reading the groups map and saving would start losing expenses, and the suite only fires two or three concurrent writes, so it might not notice.
